correctness.rationale: Exact description of all matchings by at most one first-terminal and one second-terminal edge, plus available disjoint middle edges. Acyclic Boolean-fiber toggles yield the critical cell counts (one 0-cell; two 1-cells for b=2; three 0- and 2a+1 one-cells for b=1); connectivity and Euler characteristic finish the integral graph homotopy. For b>=3 the unique critical vertex gives simplicial collapse. The b=0 case is the connected bipartite graph with 2a vertices and a(a-1) edges, except a=2 two components. Standalone verifier independently enumerates 40 instances and verifies matching acyclicity and mod-two ranks.

originality.rationale: The public quadrilateral-book result implies the homotopy types in the special a=0 subfamily by adding a terminal edge whose matching vertex cones over the contractible middle-edge simplex; this known overlap is expressly credited. Neither the inspected cycle-chain/outerplanar papers nor the quadrilateral-book result implies the exact classification for arbitrary positive numbers a of length-two arms, including the 2a-1 rank law and two-circle plateau. Explicit all-parameter acyclic matching supplies the new full phase diagram. Residual unindexed-literature risk remains.

value.rationale: A complete natural two-parameter topological phase diagram for nonouterplanar multi-theta graphs, where adding a third three-edge path kills every homotopy class by explicit elementary collapse. The universal b=2 rank-two plateau, b=1 linearly growing circle rank and b=0 chessboard rank are a structurally motivated boundary not determined by existing qualitative sphere-wedge theorems. The precise two-pole short-arm model is relevant to failures of extending outerplanar matching-complex classification to nonouterplanar planar graphs. The previously known zero-short-arm book subfamily alone gives no information about the a-dependent homology when length-two arms are present.
